question_text: Draw the inductor voltage and inductor current waveforms alongside the high-side gate control signal. Why do they look like this?
answer_text: The voltage is a square wave alternating between positive and negative. The current is a continuous triangle wave.
explanation_text: This perfectly visualizes V = L(di/dt). When the switch is ON, a positive flat voltage (V_in - V_out) is applied across the inductor, causing current to ramp up diagonally. When OFF, the switch node drops to ~0V, so the voltage across the inductor becomes negative (-V_out). This constant negative voltage causes the current to ramp down diagonally.
bonus_question_text: In steady-state, what is the average voltage across the inductor over a full switching cycle?
bonus_answer_text: Exactly zero volts. This is the principle of Volt-Second Balance.
